responses.value: Convert the lane. Buses carry 18,000 riders a day, and each would save 8 minutes, against 2 minutes lost by each of 22,000 people in cars, so total travel time falls sharply, for $3M. The main risk is opposition from 40 shops worried about parking, though 70% of their customers arrive on foot or by bus. The next step is a 6-month pilot with loading zones that measures trip times and shop sales.
Update. At 8 minutes each, the 22,000 in cars lose about 176,000 minutes a day, more than the 144,000 bus riders save, so I'd make it peak-hours only.
